purpose: Small parent context radii and approximate reflected-flux inputs; no new parent scene package or surface map.

parents.radiusConvention: Cube root of product of semiaxes: volume-equivalent radius of the inferred mean ellipsoid. Published rounded spherical diameter is 113 km.
parents.sizeUncertainty: No independent formal axis errors attached to this numerical ellipsoid in the checked passage. Figures depend on occultation and light-curve model assumptions.

sizeSource.title: Buie et al. (2015), Size and shape from stellar occultation observations of the double Jupiter Trojan Patroclus and Menoetius
sizeSource.selection: Published mean-ellipsoidal full axes 127 × 117 × 98 km for Patroclus. Not the 124.6 × 98.2 km projected limb and not the unresolved system thermal diameter.
sizeSource.release: Published numerical facts; no figure or texture copied.

parents.photometryAssumption: The NEOWISE record is for the unresolved Patroclus–Menoetius system. Apply its visible geometric albedo to the primary as an explicit common-albedo point-photometry approximation; this is not a resolved primary albedo measurement. The system equivalent thermal diameter 140.362 km is not used for the primary radius.
parents.gmSource: Menoetius source/validation/epoch-state.json and its retained Patroclus Horizons source response, prepared by Jupiter lane.

parents.referenceRadius: Preserve existing Moshup BODIES value and original archived Alpha mesh scale.
parents.photometryAssumption: Whole-system optical visible geometric albedo, applied to the primary as a common-albedo point-photometry approximation. Paper value uses the original radar primary shape and observed mean aspect; not a surface albedo texture.

parents.referenceRadius: Preserve existing Sylvia BODIES value and source-selected MPCD shape scale.
parents.photometryAssumption: Adopt current JPL SBDB selection citing NEOWISE Mainzer et al. (2014). Unresolved radiometry is primary-dominated; use only approximate point photometry and retain shape-derived physical radius rather than replacing it with thermal diameter.
